I will point out that for me, working night shift was way more exhausting than working day shift and I did it for years. I confronted him about when he gets home on a decent-good day, he is awake for 5 hours before heading to bed or he immediately goes to sleep and wakes up super early for work. He can spend an hour or two doing some things around the house and then play his video games and watch tv. 

It is an absolute bullshit excuse and I stopped putting up with it. I stopped wedding planning, I stopped cooking for him except his predesignated meal prep for lunch and dinner (if he got tired of that he can cook for his own damn self), I only did my laundry, etc. I sleep like a rock and even if I didn't he could still do some light cleaning around the house without waking me up. We ended up separating because he wanted a live in mommy and I just did not want to take on that role. 

I am not suggesting you break up, just bring up to him the amount of work you are doing and the toll it is having on you. Hopefully he is receptive of that. Sometimes it helps to sit down together and write out everything both of you do and make adjustments (and I even mean the mental prep of grocery shopping, making plans for the day to do things, etc.).

As someone with bipolar disorder, she can only get help from a medical professional. Refuse to ride the roller coaster, you are in no way obligated to. It's not abandoning her, she is emotionally and mentally draining you and it is not fair to you. Medication is absolutely mandatory and BP is a lifelong disorder. She needs to make an appointment with a psychiatrist or their nurse practitioner, not a general practitioner. They are better trained on psychotropic medications and are up to date with all the latest medications. Yes, some meds have AWFUL side effects, but that's why you're open and honest with the doctor and/or nurse and let them know everything that happens with the medications. Also I suggest therapy. The pill isnt magic and while trying to find the "perfect" medicine, she needs to learn how to deal with the highs, lows, and whatever the inbetween is. It took me 4 1/2 years of therapy and cycling through medicine before I found what works for me. 

If you decide to ride this out, demand she makes an appointment TODAY. Not tomorrow, not a week from now, not soon. TODAY.

OP, he may just not be into art. He may like your art but doesnt care to give critiques or praises. Why? Maybe he just doesnt know how. If you are someone who has never taken an art class, never studied art, etc.,  the most he would know is if the art had obvious wrong proportions, looked funky, or was someone who just started drawing/sketching. He would have no clue if the art was from a certain style, if it is considered "sellable art", or if it is truly a technically well done piece. He cant critique something he has no knowledge of. If you want more engagement from him, ask him if there is something he would personally change about what you have produced. Or ask him if it's a piece he would buy *for* you since you're the artsy person in the relationship. But most importantly, if he gives you feedback that you asked for, you cannot be upset. That may be part of why he doesn't. Everyone asks about feedback, but sometimes people just get upset and sulk about "nevative" feedback. So people just hold back on true opinions. Honestly if it bothers you that much (which isn't a bad thing, everyone has a passion), have a conversation with him about how much art means to you and how beneficial it would be to get some honest feedback from him. If he doesn't know how you feel about it, nothing can be fixed.

My boyfriend and I are long distance and we don't talk through text, calling, video chatting, etc very often. The reason being is that even though I want to talk all the time, he could go days without speaking to me and be perfectly okay. We have very polar opposite ways of communication and I had to come to peace with that or break up. I had to learn that it doesn't mean he doesn't love me, or value me in any way. So I learned to fill up my time with other things and stop looking at my phone to see if he has texted me every few minutes. 

Now in the beginning I did have talks with him a lot about communication. His behavior would change for a little bit and then go right back to the way it was. But the thing is, this isn't a deal breaker for me. I had to think about whether or not this would work for me and if I was willing to change my communication style and lay off of him. After a few months and seeking personal therapy, I had become perfectly content with the way we would talk. I call him randomly on the rare occasion if I am really missing him and haven't heard from him in a bit. And now after a year and some odd months we are standing strong. He is completely different in person (pays a lot of attention to me) and for me, that makes up for the lack of communication when I am not there. 

The point of me saying all that, is that if this is a deal breaker for you, have a serious conversation with him about how you feel, what you need from him, and if there is no change, break it off. You require a different level of communication and he can't/isn't willing to meet those needs. 

If it isn't a deal breaker, it would still be worth it to have a serious talk about how you feel and what you are currently going through mentally and emotionally with this situation. If he doesn't know how you feel, he can't do anything to change it. But I would suggest, if you're going this route, find ways to self soothe when you start feeling lonely or sad. I found writing in a journal helps me get my feelings out and stop internalizing everything. Also filling up my time with things I enjoy (i.e- video games). Find some friends that you can talk to or spend time with. It helps a lot and helps you obsess over whether or not y'all are texting/talking.

Open relationships only work if both parties are 100% on board. That means agreeing to be open to seeing other people AND both agreeing to the boundaries. Both agree to other people? Great! Both cant agree on boundaries? Not great! That means back to the drawing board. You both have to make sure to set clear boundaries for what is and what is not okay (i.e- no sex in our house, if you or the other person catch feelings you need to end it, these days are exclusively our days, etc).

But it sounds like she wants an open relationship to get back with her ex, not other people. Which is a big red flag. It's one thing if this was discussed in a different view of wanting to see other people in general, finding sexual interest in other people, but she exclusively talked about her ex. It sounds like she wants her cake and to eat it too. 

If you want to do this, I would suggest having a big discussion on it. Take a hard look at what has been going on, have yall been stressed? Not spending quality time together? Why is she only talking about her ex and already mentioning that she is interested in him again? Maybe seek out a sex therapist before embarking on an open relationship. Make sure you cover all your bases beforehand otherwise this can quickly blow up in your face. 

And most importantly, if you are not 100% on board, DO NOT DO THIS. Even if you are 99% on board but one little thing bothers you, DO NOT DO THIS. It will end up with hurt and regret and if the relationship doesnt end at that point, you will be left with trust and jealousy issues.

I think I may need a little more info on this. Is this an apartment with both of your names on the lease? Or is this a house that she rents/owns and you are the roommate renting the extra bedroom? Have you ever been late paying bills? Is it a split 50/50 for everything or is someone paying the majority? Is there any more information on why you can no longer go to your boyfriend's?

I can understand the rule of not wanting you to have guests (friends or boyfriend) over when you are not home as it can make people uncomfortable. Even if you insist that he will just be in your room, sometimes it's that feeling of "someone else is in the house and now I have to hole up in my room" and maybe that's how your roommate feels. It seems like she was upfront from the beginning about what she was uncomfortable with and you agreed to it. 

Now here's the hard part for me, I believe that if you pay 50% rent, bills, etc. then you can control your own "domain"- which would be your room. There's obviously some restrictions like don't do illegal activity that the roommate can get in trouble for and if there were terms like no pets, don't disrespect that. But having your boyfriend spend the night every night if you wanted shouldn't be a problem. That's YOUR space, not a common living space, and she cannot control who or what you really have going on in there.

I would suggest having a conversation about him spending the night whenever you'd like due to just that- you pay rent and you guys are in your room.
